name: Angela Merkel
summary: A centre-right Christian Democrat known for pragmatic, consensus-seeking government. She combined a market-oriented, fiscally cautious economic line with acceptance of the welfare state, strong support for European integration, free trade and multilateralism, and became associated with the 2011 nuclear phase-out and the 2015 refugee intake. On social questions she held moderately conservative personal views while allowing liberalising change.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Her 2006 health reform made health insurance compulsory for all residents, keeping Germany's universal contribution-funded system rather than expanding private purchase.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Her conservatives long opposed a national minimum wage, favouring sector deals; she then accepted and implemented an 8.50 euro statutory minimum as the SPD's coalition condition. No record of seeking a substantial raise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Backed the Agenda 2010 labour-market reforms, pressed Greece to privatise, and called free international trade the foundation of prosperity; she works within the social market economy rather than pure market doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: During the euro crisis she pushed Greece toward privatising state assets such as regional airports; no record of seeking public ownership of industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In the 2013 coalition talks she blocked the SPD's demand for higher taxes on the rich.

strong-leader.rationale: Drawing on life in the GDR, she told Harvard graduates that democracy and individual liberties are not givens and must be defended; she governed through coalitions and parliament.

state-harmful.rationale: A career head of government who argued for strong democratic institutions; no hint of anti-statism.

empower-police-military.rationale: Her government suspended conscription in 2011 and shrank the Bundeswehr, a downsizing later criticised after 2022; no explicit statement on police powers found.

traditional-family.rationale: Voted against same-sex marriage because she holds marriage to be between a man and a woman, yet said same-sex couples should be able to adopt jointly; moderately traditional.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Allowed a free conscience vote that legalised same-sex marriage in 2017, but personally voted no, citing the Basic Law's definition of marriage as between man and woman, while asking for respect for the other view.

abortion-legal.rationale: Described as personally opposed to abortion; she abstained in 1992 on a bill allowing abortion up to the 12th week rather than voting against it.

more-religion-public.rationale: A professing Protestant who said in 2012 that Germany suffers from too little Christianity rather than too much Islam; she has not pushed for religion to shape laws.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said the multicultural 'live side by side' approach had utterly failed and that immigrants must integrate and learn German, while also saying mosques are part of Germany's landscape.

gradual-change.rationale: Generally incremental, consensus-based governing within existing institutions, though with abrupt turns such as the 2011 nuclear phase-out and the 2015 border decision.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Kept the borders open in 2015 and in her memoir still rejects blame; argues Germany's ageing workforce makes legal migration essential. She also backed the 2016 EU-Turkey deal to curb irregular arrivals.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Argued that thinking and action must be multilateral rather than unilateral; central to the Lisbon Treaty strengthening EU institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Said protectionism and trade conflicts jeopardise free international trade and thus the foundation of prosperity.

nation-first.rationale: Called for multilateral rather than unilateral action and an outward-looking rather than isolationist stance.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

open-borders.rationale: In her memoir she writes that Europe must always protect its external borders, while defending openness to refugees in 2015.

limit-growth.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls human-made climate change a threat requiring collective action and pledged carbon neutrality by 2050; backed the Energiewende, though her 2019 package was widely criticised as too weak.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Sees major benefits from technologies such as AI but insists humans must set the rules for technology and centre human dignity; neither techno-optimist nor sceptic on the record found.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Decided the nuclear phase-out after Fukushima in 2011; in her memoir she says Germany does not need nuclear power to meet climate goals.

notes: Born 17 July 1954; living as of the audit (no death date recorded). Positions shifted over time: she opposed then implemented a statutory minimum wage, extended then ended nuclear power (2011), and moved to support joint adoption by same-sex couples while still voting against same-sex marriage. Many statements in this test (e.g. land-value tax, drug policy, gun control, sex work, encryption) have no recorded position in the sources consulted and are left null rather than inferred from CDU membership.
